newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to renew MFN for China - U.S. officials.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to renew MFN for China - U.S. officials.

text.p: President Bill Clinton is expected to renew most favored nation trade status for China for another year on Monday, U.S. officials said.
Congress will vote on whether to overturn his decision.

The officials told Reuters that Clinton would announce his decision later in the day and Secretary of State Madeleine Albright would make the case for the administration position during an appearance in Delaware.

"The president is going to announce MFN today," one administration official said. Renewing favourable trade benefits for China "is very much in the national interest and we will push very hard for it on the Hill (with Congress) and with (American) public opinion," he added.
Favourable trade benefits for China are controversial, and some members of Congress have already made clear their intention to try to overturn the decision.

Clinton, who has agreed to a summit with Chinese President Jiang Zemin later this year, has worked hard to improve ties with Beijing. But China's human rights record, its sale of missiles and technology to other countries and its huge trade surplus with the United States remain major problems.
